newsitem.title: MEXICO: Radio Centro wins telecomms concession.
newsitem.headline: Radio Centro wins telecomms concession.

text.p: Amaritel, a consortium of companies led by Mexican media firm Radio Centro, has won a concession to provide local and long-distance telephone service in Mexico, Radio Centro said in a statement on Monday.

"The concession represents the first concession granted to a wireline telephone operating company to provide both local and long distance service following the deregulation of the Mexican telecommunications market," it said.
Grupo Radio Centro will be the controlling entity of Amaritel.
U.S. Global Telecommunications Inc, a subsidiary of U.S. Telecom Holdings Inc., will hold a 49 percent stake in the venture.
Another Mexican firm, Advance Telecom SA, will also participate in the capital of Amaritel and be a consultant. The statement did not say how much capital Advance Telecom would provide.
In addition to long distance, Amaritel will provide local service in 111 communities in Mexico, about 25 percent of the population, and develop 250,000 access lines.

"It is anticipated that an investment of $70 million in equity will be required during the initial build-out, of which $14 million will be invested by Radio Centro and US Telecom Holdings divided approximately equally between them," it said.
Radio Centro operates and/or owns 15 radio stations in Mexico. U.S. Telecom Holdings is involved in telephone and network projects in Hungary and the Czech Republic.
